Write the ApplyLateFees use case for a freelancer invoicing app. It runs every night.

An invoice is eligible when it is sent (not paid, not disputed) and more than 5 days past its due date. The fee is 1.5% of the original invoice amount for every started 30-day period since the due date; a period is only charged once, even if the job runs again. Total late fees on an invoice can never exceed 10% of the original amount. When a fee is added, notify the client. Return how many invoices were charged and the total added.

Implement the BookDesk use case for our co-working space.

- Bookings are whole hours. A booking starts at 08:00 or later, ends at 20:00 at the latest and lasts 1 to 4 hours.
- It must start in the future, in the space's local time.
- It cannot overlap another booking on the same desk.
- A member can hold at most 2 upcoming bookings.
- Members on the day-pass plan can only book for the current day; monthly members can book any day.

Implement the use case that distributes the tip pool of a restaurant shift.

- Only a closed shift can be distributed, and only once.
- Front of house gets 70% of the pool (rounded to the nearest cent), back of house the rest.
- Within each group the share is proportional to minutes worked, rounded down to the cent; leftover cents go to the person with the most minutes in that group (ties: lowest employee id).
- Managers and anyone who worked less than 60 minutes are excluded.
- If one group has nobody eligible, the whole pool goes to the other group. If nobody is eligible at all, the distribution fails.

Implement the PledgeToCampaign use case for a crowdfunding platform.

A backer pledges an amount, optionally choosing a reward tier. The campaign must be live (now between launch and deadline, deadline exclusive) and not cancelled. Minimum pledge is 5.00. A chosen tier requires the pledge to be at least the tier's minimum and the tier to have units left; limited tiers lose one unit per pledge. Creators cannot back their own campaign, and a backer can pledge only once per campaign. The pledged amount is only authorized on the backer's card now (captured at the deadline if the goal is met); if the authorization is declined, nothing is saved.

Write a use case that triages a newly filed insurance claim and assigns it to a queue.

1. The policy must exist and be active on the incident date (between start and end, and not cancelled before the incident). An incident date in the future is invalid.
2. Fraud indicators: reported more than 30 days after the incident, incident within 14 days of the policy start, or 3 or more earlier claims on the same policy in the last 12 months. Any indicator sends the claim to special investigation, listing the indicators.
3. Without indicators: claimed amount up to 1,000.00 is fast-tracked, above 25,000.00 goes to a senior adjuster, everything else to the standard queue.

We need a use case that processes a cycle count submitted by a warehouse counter for one bin and SKU.

- The bin cannot be counted while it has open pick tasks.
- The counted quantity must be a whole number, zero or more.
- Variance = counted − system quantity. Tolerance is the larger of 2 units or 1% of the system quantity.
- Variance within tolerance: the stock is adjusted immediately (a zero variance is just a match).
- Variance above tolerance on the first count: no adjustment, the bin is flagged for a recount.
- On the recount: if the absolute variance valued at unit cost is at most 500.00 the stock is adjusted; above that the adjustment goes to a supervisor for approval and the stock stays unchanged.
- Every adjustment is written to the inventory ledger.
